opencode.notes: Default advisory provider: runs with zero credentials on free models, and its model family is independent of Claude. Three traps, all measured on 1.15.6 — (1) a denied write can hang past 2m30s, so --agent plan plus a hard timeout are both required; (2) without --pure it loads the user's global MCP servers and will route around a write denial through them; (3) it spawns its own subagents unless permission.task is denied.

codex.notes: Strongest agentic option and the only provider offering patch-proposal. Requires a ChatGPT sign-in. Runs under --sandbox read-only for advisory and repository-read; patch-proposal asks for a unified diff in the prompt and still forbids applying it.

agy.auth_error_pattern: (IneligibleTier|UNSUPPORTED_CLIENT|please sign in|not signed in|authentication required|authentication failed|authentication timed out)
agy.notes: Large context and multimodal input; authenticates through the system keyring, never an API key. Two silent failure modes — omitting --add-dir makes it scan its own scratch dir and report the repo as empty, and an unknown --model does not error, it falls back to the default model and exits 0. The model string must be an exact display label from `agy models`. UNLIKE opencode and codex, agy has no independently verified read-only enforcement: `--dangerously-skip-permissions` disables its own guardrails outright, so "no writes" in repository-read mode is a prompt-level request, not a policy the CLI enforces. `--mode plan` is set on every invocation because `agy --help` documents it as a distinct read-only execution mode (the same shape as opencode's `--agent plan`), but that has only been confirmed as an accepted flag, not measured end-to-end against a signed-in session — treat it as best-effort, not a guarantee. An unauthenticated run prints an OAuth URL and blocks INTERACTIVELY for up to 60s waiting for an authorization code before failing with "Authentication required... Error: authentication timed out / authentication failed or timed out" — in a headless run that is a minute of dead wall-clock before auth_error_pattern ever gets a chance to classify it, on top of whatever `--timeout` this run was given. `probeProvider` reports `agy` as available whenever the binary is on PATH — CLI session state cannot be probed for free — so "available: true" for `agy` means installed, not authenticated or usable.

kimi.notes: Long-context synthesis and multilingual review. Unavailable until KIMI_API_KEY is exported.

deepseek.notes: Cheap independent review. Unavailable until DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is exported.

local-openai.notes: The only provider permitted to receive privacy.classification=restricted, because execution is local-only. Points at Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint by default; LOCAL_OPENAI_API_KEY is optional and defaults to a placeholder. Set LOCAL_OPENAI_BASE_URL to mark it available.
